question: On 18 June 2026, the Commission sent information to Parliament’s Committee on Budgets concerning an undertaking given during the G7 summit to provide EUR 75 million towards the restoration of the New Safe Confinement, the Chornobyl sarcophagus. The Committee on Budgets has already indicated that this is contrary to paragraph 39 of the new Framework Agreement on relations between the European Parliament and the European Commission1. With this in mind: 1.
Is it common for the Commission to take a decision before consulting Parliament in accordance with the rules in force?
Was the Commission in a hurry in this particular case, or did its President come under any pressure from the G7 to reach this decision?2
Does the Commission still see the value in interinstitutional consultation and in following official procedures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.8.2026) On 14 February 2025, a Russian drone strike hit and severely damaged the New Safe Confinement (NSC) at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant that covers the damaged unit 4. The damage poses serious risks to nuclear safety with potential consequences in Ukraine and beyond, including in the EU.

In order to mitigate the risk of radioactive contamination, urgent repairs to the NSC must be implemented as soon as possible. Further work is also required to establish and implement long term repairs, which will ensure nuclear and radiation safety from within the NSC and enable safe decommissioning of the damaged unit 4.

In the context of this urgency, the Commission has thus pledged EUR 75 million in grant funding as its contribution to nuclear safety, preparedness, environmental protection and international cooperation and is urging European and G7 partners to follow suit.

The Commission values the cooperation with the European Parliament, which is why the Commission sent information to European Parliament’s Committee on Budgets regarding this undertaking, in line with usual arrangements.
